shortcut_name: Steiner-tree reduction with redundant non-target constraint
evidence: gpt-oss-120b uses a terminal-mask DP: "full = (1 << t) - 1" and "dp = [[INF] * n for _ in range(1 << t)]". This is the standard minimum Steiner-tree approach.
affordance_in_statement: The active index set S is "the union of the target set T and the set of all indices ... in at least one vector in C"; the selected vectors must have dimension and cardinality exactly "|S| - 1"; every cost satisfies "1 ≤ w ≤ 1000000".
removal_suggestion: Make the non-target participation condition non-redundant by requiring each non-target index to occur in at least two selected vectors, with at least one of those vectors having a target index as its other endpoint. The sample selections still satisfy this, but an ordinary Steiner-tree DP no longer captures feasibility.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Reduces the algebraic conditions to a minimum-cost Steiner tree connecting the targets; positive costs and the definition of S make non-target leaves removable, so the degree condition is effectively automatic.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The vectors have the form "b_u - b_v", while dimension and cardinality are both exactly "|S| - 1" and costs are positive.

common_affordance: The problem can be solved as a positive-weight minimum Steiner tree on the graph whose edges are the candidate vectors; the explicit non-target degree condition does not prevent pruning non-target leaves.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The implementation is incomplete or truncated after beginning the spanning-tree interpretation, causing a runtime error rather than producing an answer.
It attempts exhaustive subset or combination enumeration, which is too slow under the stated bounds and times out instead of using a terminal-mask Steiner DP.
Its graph optimization does not correctly preserve all of the active-set, exact-cardinality, and non-target participation conditions, leading to an incorrect answer.

recommended_edit: Replace the current non-target condition with a terminal-incidence condition: every non-target active index must occur in at least two selected vectors, and at least one such vector must connect it directly to a target index. This preserves the examples while defeating the plain Steiner-tree reduction.
regression_risk: The edit may make the already-defeated MST-style solutions appear closer to correct on instances where every non-target has a direct target neighbor; add hidden cases containing non-target chains to protect against that regression.
